meta.uses: scripts/fallback_sim.py (slicing, Ozaki-II truncation and CRT, rounding, generators)
meta.sampling: none: every entry of every 256 x 256 output is simulated (65,536 per GEMM)

ozaki1_lists.rule: slicesForCR: [s0, s0+1], s0 = slicesFor 11 (53 + clog2 k)

cost_model.mm_unit: A tile product is one TM x TN output tile times one slice or residue product of inner dimension k on the matrix multiplier. With 11-bit slices, split-K runs chunks of 4 products with one mma.m16n8k16 per chunk (OzakiTC SliceRun.blocks), so a 16x8 tile product is ceil(k/4) MMA instructions. dot_products_per_entry = tile products x TM TN / (m n), the number of dot products of length k per output entry.
cost_model.C: The per-entry costs of fallback_sim (prefix reuse, an exact fallback of s_e^2 minus the reused pairs, +1 for the zero-aware indicator product), summed and divided by TM TN.
cost_model.A: The level of an entry is the first level at which its rounding test succeeds (the exact fallback if none does), and the level of a tile is the largest level of its entries; the tile pays the cumulative cost of that level, with S = max s_e in the tile for the exact fallback.
cost_model.A_shuffled: A on tiles of uniformly permuted entries (no correlation inside a tile).
cost_model.B_ideal: Level 0 runs on all tiles; level l runs on ceil(#failed/TM TN) tiles, where #failed counts the entries whose rounding test failed at every earlier level; the exact fallback runs on the entries sorted by s_e, packed TM TN per tile, each tile paying its max s_e.
cost_model.B_gather: As B_ideal, but a tile is TM gathered rows x TN gathered columns (an outer product) covering the entries whose rounding test failed, with a greedy schedule (see the docstring).
cost_model.adaptive: A tile (A, B) or entry (C) with S^2 at most the cost of the first rounding test goes straight to the exact fallback (ozaki1CRA).
cost_model.baselines: exact_tile: S^2 per tile; exact_entry: sum s_e^2 / TM TN; exact_global: (max s_e)^2 per tile.
cost_model.off_mm: Work off the matrix multiplier: slicing once per matrix to the depth an issued product needs; accumulation of useful products only (masked entries skip it); rounding tests on whole tiles for A and on the entries still undecided for B and C; Ozaki-II conversion of the rows and columns involved per configuration, and CRT per modulus for each reconstructed entry (whole tiles for A).
cost_model.survival: The fraction of the per-entry absolute saving that policy X keeps: (exact_tile - X) / (exact_tile - C) (like for like: both tiled) and (exact_entry - X) / (exact_entry - C) (conservative: early exit pays tile costs while the exact-fallback baseline is charged per entry); 1 = all kept, <= 0 = none; null when early exit per entry saves less than 0.5 %.

meta.caveats: A model of issued instructions and 64-bit integer operations, not GPU time; memory traffic, gathers, latency and occupancy are not modelled; the input distributions are chosen; entries of one GEMM share rows and columns, so their outcomes are correlated (A_shuffled shows the uncorrelated case).
